parsed.explanation: No trans offence, entry/custody targeting or care ban is documented, and a delayed torture conviction shows some recourse. The dominant exposure is a national birth/biological-sex public-restroom ban, including trans youth, with no documented working remedy, no current gender-identity hate-crime/anti-discrimination protection, documented rising hate crime and institutional discrimination. That is an unremedied universal-exposure measure, placing it in Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.interaction: Resident name/marker processes do not establish visitor passport treatment; no border mismatch rule is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Historical police torture/sexual abuse of a trans woman, convicted nearly 20 years later; no current visitordetention, search or placement rule documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Three officers sentenced to 17 years, first such conviction, showing eventual prosecution.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Delayed remedy does not document current custody safety or placement for a detained visitor.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: May/April 2025 laws restrict public restrooms by birth/biological sex, bar identity-congruent access including trans youth, and ban inclusive signage; framed as harassment risk.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No working remedy reversing the facility rule is documented; a venue staff conviction for denying entry is a separate service case.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National rule applies in transit/public spaces regardless of local tolerance; hotel/private alternatives do not cure the public-facility exclusion.

care_services.exposure: One regional hospital mistreatment complaint pending; no emergency ward or medication rule documented.
care_services.protection: Pathologising terminology removed in 2024, 'gender discordance' used, and sexual orientation/gender identity reiterated as not diseases.
care_services.interaction: Health terminology reform is a climate/protection signal but does not offset the operative restroom restriction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Legislators/officials frame trans people as harassment risks and use child-protection pretext; vague censorship articles and a 2025 NGO-registration law risk weaponisation against queer organising.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A July 2025 court ruled an anti-equality decree unconstitutional; same-sex conduct is lawful and trans identity is not an offence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing increases hostile interactions from the facility ban; no documented police sweeps, extortion or presentation arrests.

minors_guardians.exposure: Restroom laws explicitly bar trans youth from identity-congruent facilities; child-protection articles enable censorship of identity content.
minors_guardians.protection: Age of consent is 14 irrespective of orientation/gender, and conversion therapy is banned for medical professionals.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces the same facility exclusion; no documented minor care denial, detention or custody rule.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A 2024 report finds hate crimes rose with trans women most affected, magnitude unquantified; public hostility accompanies restrictions.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Historical torture case ultimately prosecuted; venue staff were sentenced for denying trans women entry.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No current gender-identity hate-crime protection is in force, so street/service hostility has thin documented recourse, despite occasional convictions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No operative anti-discrimination/hate-crime protection on gender identity is in force; public institutions are described as contributing to anti-LGBTIQ discrimination.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have produced occasional remedies, including the torture conviction and rulings against an anti-equality decree.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are episodic/delayed and none is documented as changing the national restroom rule, so recourse cannot be credited as working for that exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 birth-sex facility regime with courts failing to provide relief, but this dossier lacks its documented emergency-ward rule and routine document-checking, so it sits somewhat above 0.35.

Closest: a birth-sex bathroom rule without a presentation offence and with polite/private alternatives. This dossier rates lower because hate crime is rising, institutions contribute to discrimination, and no gender-identity hate protection is in force.
Higher because there is no universal facility exclusion and remedies demonstrably corrected refusals. Here the facility ban is national, recent and unremedied, so it sits materially below 0.65.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is not criminalisation or organised targeting, but a nationally imposed, identity-based facility exclusion affecting every outed visitor, including minors, reinforced by state threat-framing and absent hate-crime protection. Occasional prosecutions and health-terminology reforms show courts can act, yet no documented remedy has displaced the restroom rule. That combination is an unremedied universal exposure in Elevated Risk, below 0.45, above 0.35 because custody, ward placement, border targeting and extortion are not documented.
